description: Interested in engineering, web design, and space
summary: Mission Builder is a browser game where players, solo or in teams of up to four, design a complete space mission by choosing an orbit, rocket, power, communications and instruments. A live dashboard shows how each choice affects mass, power, budget and data, and a post-launch report explains why the mission succeeded or failed.
details:
The player can use Mission Builder to design, play and analyse their own space mission. The player will need to select a scenario for their mission (Monitoring Earth’s climate, searching for Ice on the Moon or Weather monitoring on Mars). Then choose an orbit, launch vehicle, solar panels, communication dish, science equipment and mission duration. The game has a live mission planner which shows what your mass, power, budget, data and science capabilities are compared to your limits. Every element effects each other, a larger communication dish will increase your data capability but also increase your mass, power and budget. The further away your orbit, the less sunlight you will get meaning your radio speed will be slower. When the player launches their mission it will check if the rocket can carry your spacecraft, randomly generate an event (Solar flare, ground station issue, rocket shake or quiet mission) and give a report about their mission. It will give you a score out of 100 and explain simply why your mission was successful or not. There isn’t one ‘perfect’ answer meaning it teaches the player about compromises. The player can play alone or with a team of up to 4 people. Each role (Mission Lead, Spacecraft Engineer, Science Lead and Ops and Budget) have their own section of the design to complete and have their own aim. These aims can conflict meaning the team will have to negotiate. The team can only play by passing the screen.

We created the game using HTML, CSS and JavaScript. This meant it was all in one file with no framework or backend meaning it can be played on any browser. This includes phones and doesn’t require any downloads or logins. We used an AI assistant (Claude) to help us with our coding. The physics are simple to understand for beginners but realistic. Each mission has a different constraint (Budget for earth, mass for moon and power and rocket size for Mars). The random events reward the player for having good margins. We want to help students to see how everything works together in a mission and feel like engineering is something they can have a go at. In the future we would include online multiplayer, more scenarios, sandbox mode and shared designs.
